purpose: Machine-readable provenance dossier binding every load-bearing claim in the Emender paper to committed artifacts (results CSVs/JSON, figures, Lean theorem sources, eval CSVs), so the paper can point readers at a 'committed run artifacts' surface. Each artifact records the path, the most recent commit that touched it (git -C /home/erikg/emender-paper log --format=%h -1 -- <path>), and what the artifact shows.

claims.claim: The Emender/E88 1.273B pure-nonlinear-recurrent LM (dim=1664, depth=12, H=370, N=32) reaches 0.973 bits-per-byte on The Pile after ~22-24 GPU-days on a single workstation-class GPU, with no cluster and no sequence parallelism.

artifacts.shows: Normalized 100K-trailing nats/bpb vs wallclock trajectory for the E88 v0.3 run; endpoint 0.973 BPB at step 1,542,000.
Records the v0.3 checkpoint steps and 100K-trailing loss/bpb endpoints for E88/GDN/M2RNN-CMA with per-model configs and the bpb conversion constant.

Measured 7,492 tok/s sustained and 99.8% median GPU utilization for E88 1.273B on an RTX 6000 Ada; substantiates the single-GPU throughput/viability route.

claims.claim: The throughput comes from width-axis multi-programming: 22,200 small bounded recurrent programs per token (370 heads x batch 5 x depth 12), each a 32x32 matrix-state tile held in registers, with the time loop serial inside each program.

unbound_claims.gap: No Lean module ElmanProofs/Architectures/EmenderLatching.lean exists in the worktree, the theorems are absent from the PaperCore import closure, and no such path appears anywhere in this worktree's git history. The cited names appear only in paper main.typ and paper/data/math-notation-spec.md. The three latching theorems cited by the paper are not backed by any committed Lean source here.

unbound_claims.claim: The Triton multi-programming kernel runs identically on CUDA and ROCm.
unbound_claims.gap: No ROCm/AMD test or benchmark is committed. paper/review/THROUGHPUT.md measures an RTX 6000 Ada (CUDA) only. There is no committed artifact demonstrating ROCm parity.

unbound_claims.claim: The within-class ordering recorded by the single 1.3B racer trajectory is replicated across four independent CMA-ES sweeps spanning 250+ candidate configurations per architecture.
unbound_claims.gap: No committed per-sweep artifact enumerates four CMA-ES sweeps at 250+ configs/architecture. The aggregated burst dataset (paper/results/cmaes_burst_v2) covers 1,285 configurations total across 13 architecture-family panels but is not decomposed into the claimed four 250+ sweeps. The claim is only asserted in the paper caption and in the paper/review/rigor.md audit note.

unbound_claims.claim: The three 1.3B-class checkpoints, the per-architecture CMA-ES configurations, and the Triton multi-programming kernel are released to the HuggingFace v0.3 target.
unbound_claims.gap: No checkpoint or release manifest is committed in this worktree; the v0.3 weights and CMA-ES configs live off-repo (HuggingFace / ~/elman). The Appendix B readback (Emender 0.96613 / GDN 0.96612 / M2RNN-CMA 0.96132) is documented but the released artifacts themselves are not in-repo.

notes: Status values: 'bound' = at least one committed artifact exists at a known commit; 'bound-partial' = a committed artifact exists but a sub-claim's raw run data or an auxiliary measurement is not committed; 'unbound' = no committed artifact. Commit hashes are the most-recent commit touching each path (git log --format=%h -1 -- <path>), not necessarily the commit that first added it. The paper source is Typst (paper/main.typ), not LaTeX.
